examples.question_text:
Find each probability in the form given.
a. $P(\text{win})=\frac{17}{25}$. Find $P(\text{not win})$ as a fraction in simplest form.
b. $P(\text{late})=0.37$. Find $P(\text{not late})$ as a decimal.
c. $P(\text{on time})=82\%$. Find $P(\text{not on time})$ as a percentage.
examples.solution_text:
An event and its complement have probabilities that add to $1$.
a. $P(\text{not win})=1-\frac{17}{25}=\frac{8}{25}$
b. $P(\text{not late})=1-0.37=0.63$
c. $1=100\%$, so $P(\text{not on time})=100\%-82\%=18\%$

examples.question_text:
A bag holds $7$ orange, $5$ blue and $9$ purple counters. One counter is chosen at random.
a. Find $P(\text{blue})$ as a fraction in simplest form.
b. Use the complement to find $P(\text{not blue})$ as a fraction in simplest form.
c. Check by counting the non-blue counters. Why can using the complement save work?
examples.solution_text:
a. There are $7+5+9=21$ counters in total.
$P(\text{blue})=\frac{5}{21}$
b. $P(\text{not blue})=1-P(\text{blue})=1-\frac{5}{21}=\frac{16}{21}$
c. There are $7+9=16$ orange or purple counters, so the check gives $\frac{16}{21}$.
Using the complement needs only the probability of blue, rather than finding and adding the probabilities of orange and purple.

examples.question_text:
a. A team wins with probability $0.27$ and loses with probability $0.38$. Every match ends in a win, loss or draw. Find the probability of a draw as a decimal.
b. A box contains only green, red and white cards. A card is chosen at random. $P(\text{green})=\frac{7}{23}$ and $P(\text{red})=\frac{6}{23}$. Find the probability of choosing neither green nor red as a fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution_text:
a. A draw is the complement of a win or a loss. These outcomes do not overlap.
$P(\text{draw})=1-(0.27+0.38)=1-0.65=0.35$
b. Neither green nor red means white. The colours do not overlap.
$P(\text{white})=1-\left(\frac{7}{23}+\frac{6}{23}\right)=1-\frac{13}{23}=\frac{10}{23}$

examples.question_text:
Every match ends in a win, loss or draw. A team wins with probability $\frac{1}{3}$ and loses with probability $\frac{1}{6}$. Let $E$ be the event that the team wins or loses.
a. Explain what $P(E')$ means in this situation.
b. Find $P(E')$ as a fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution_text:
a. $P(E')$ is the probability that the team neither wins nor loses. Since every match ends in a win, loss or draw, this is the probability of a draw.
b. Win and loss do not overlap.
$\begin{align*}P(E)&=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}\\&=\frac{2}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P(E')&=1-P(E)\\&=1-\frac{1}{2}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Win and loss are disjoint, so P(E)=1/3+1/6=2/6+1/6=3/6=1/2. The exhaustive win/loss/draw sample space makes E' the draw event. Therefore P(E')=1-P(E)=1-1/2=1/2. This follows the supplied complement rule and missing-outcome exercises.
